$comment: Every test data file outside git: the reference images and the lab's profiles, kept in E:/Photografie/Astro/code-testdata/AstroPhotoAnalyzer/ (ADR 0088). Names are relative to that folder, where TestData.LargeDir looks unless APA_TESTDATA_LARGE names another. scripts/check-testdata.ps1 verifies presence and SHA-256 in the folder APA_TESTDATA_LARGE names, which /validate sets (a missing large file is a warning locally); -Update rewrites this file with PowerShell JSON layout. The cases in docs/validation.json name these files. AstroPhotoAnalyzer has no repo fixtures: they are generated or hand-built in the tests.

files.name: de_printat.png
files.source: the owner's finished Milky Way core (E:/Photografie/Claude/de_printat.png, 103 387 067 bytes), exported from Siril; the image the tool was built to measure
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-001 to V-003; StarPairTests (Category=Validation): at least 4000 stars kept (ADR 0054)

files.name: starless_rbf0.5_stretch0.17.fit
files.source: the owner's plate-solved, starless, VeraLux-stretched FITS of the same Milky Way core (E:/Photografie/Astro/Milkyway-Core/2026-08-12-Smida/Processed_With_1mmPTFE_Flats/CropAndPlateSolve/RBF0.5/preview/, 270 869 760 bytes, 5837 x 3867, Siril 1.4.4 with a TAN-SIP WCS); the image ADR 0025 was measured on
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-004: the dust and the sky from the WCS and the LDN catalogue; StarPairTests (Category=Validation): under 20 stars (ADR 0054)

files.name: Hahnemuhle PRBaryta.icm
files.source: the ICC profile the lab Chromatone publishes for Hahnemuehle Photo Rag Baryta on its Canon iPF8300 (https://www.chromatone.ro/profile.html, assets/icc/Hahnemuhle PRBaryta.icm, 1 625 256 bytes; v2, lut16, made with MonacoPROFILER on 2012-03-07); the profile ADR 0028 took baryta's Dmax from
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-006: the Dmax read from a real v2 printer profile

files.name: HARMAN_Canvas.icc
files.source: the ICC profile the same page offers for Harman Canvas (assets/icc/HARMAN_Canvas.icc, 1 515 624 bytes; v2, lut16, made with LOGO ProfileMaker on 2010-09-07, measured with an Eye-One Pro)
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-007: a paper with a weak black, where the perceptual table would give 2.46

files.name: Rosetta_starless_no_WCS.fit
files.source: the owner's starless Rosetta nebula, stretched in Siril, 3551 x 2422, three float planes, 103 210 560 bytes, no WCS; added 2026-10-06 as the deep-sky frame the sky-relative classes were designed on (ADR 0033)
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-010 and V-011: the classes relative to the modelled sky, the dust from the darkest sky, the curves anchored on those classes; StarPairTests (Category=Validation): under 20 stars, and the starless half of the Rosetta pair (ADR 0054)

files.name: Orion_with_WCS.fit
files.source: the owner's starless Orion nebula with the Running Man (the starless export of Orion_WithStars_and_WCS.fit, at another size), stretched in Siril, 1564 x 2302, three float planes, 43 214 400 bytes, with a WCS far from the galactic plane; added 2026-10-06 as the frame whose peaks are already over the curves' target (ADR 0033)
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-012: no curve suggested, the reason naming the peaks and the target; StarPairTests (Category=Validation): under 20 stars (ADR 0054)

files.name: Veil_Starless.fit
files.source: the owner's starless Veil nebula, stretched in Siril, 5601 x 3692, three float planes, 248 158 080 bytes, with a WCS inside the galactic band (b -14.6 to -3.6 over a 9.6 x 6.4 degree field); added 2026-10-11 as the deep-sky frame the band path mistook for a Milky Way landscape (ADR 0037)
files.demonstrates: docs/validation.json V-013 and V-014: the sky path taken on a frame narrower than the band, with the reason naming its span; the curves anchored on the nebula's classes; StarPairTests (Category=Validation): under 20 stars (ADR 0054)

files.name: Rosetta_withStars_no_WCS.fit
files.source: the owner's Rosetta nebula with its stars, the frame Rosetta_starless_no_WCS.fit was made from, stretched in Siril, 3551 x 2422, three float planes, 103 210 560 bytes, no WCS, pixel-aligned with the starless frame; added 2026-10-27 as the half of the pair that labels a detection a star or grain (ADR 0054)
files.demonstrates: StarPairTests (Category=Validation): the stars kept on it, at least 99 % of them where the starless frame differs; the comparison ADR 0054's threshold was chosen on

files.name: Andromeda_WithStars_andWCS.fit
files.source: the owner's Andromeda galaxy with its stars, stretched in Siril, 3790 x 2476, three float planes, 112 622 400 bytes, with a WCS; added 2026-10-27 as a frame with stars the sigma clause must keep (ADR 0054)

files.name: Andromeda_starless_WithWCS.fit
files.source: the owner's starless Andromeda galaxy, stretched in Siril, 2623 x 1716 (a smaller export than the frame with stars, not pixel-aligned with it), three float planes, 54 023 040 bytes, with a WCS; added 2026-10-27 as a starless frame that must stay under StarMinCount (ADR 0054)

files.name: Orion_WithStars_and_WCS.fit
files.source: the owner's Orion nebula with its stars, stretched in Siril, 3908 x 2602 (a larger export than Orion_with_WCS.fit, not pixel-aligned with it), three float planes, 122 031 360 bytes, with a WCS; added 2026-10-27 as a frame with stars the sigma clause must keep (ADR 0054)

files.name: starless_rbf0.5_stretch0.1.fit
files.source: the owner's plate-solved, starless FITS of the same Milky Way core as starless_rbf0.5_stretch0.17.fit, VeraLux-stretched to a background of 0.1 instead of 0.17, 5837 x 3867, three float planes, 270 869 760 bytes; measured in ADRs 0032 and 0037, added to the manifest 2026-10-27 as a starless frame that must stay under StarMinCount (ADR 0054)
